### Pre-colonial period

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Antigua_and_Barbuda&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Pre-colonial period")]

Main article: [Pre-Columbian Antigua and Barbuda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pre-Columbian_Antigua_and_Barbuda "Pre-Columbian Antigua and Barbuda")

[Archaic-period](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archaic_period_in_Antigua_and_Barbuda "Archaic period in Antigua and Barbuda") hunter-gatherers called the [Ciboney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ciboney "Ciboney") were the first culture present in Antigua and Barbuda.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-Factbook-17)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-Britannica-22)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-Commonwealth-23)[Carbon dating](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radiocarbon_dating "Radiocarbon dating") has established the earliest settlements started around 3700 BC.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-24)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-:23-25) They were succeeded by the ceramic age pre-Columbian [Arawak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arawakan_languages "Arawakan languages")-speaking [Saladoid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saladoid "Saladoid") people who migrated from the lower [Orinoco River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orinoco_River "Orinoco River").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-26) They introduced agriculture, raising, among other crops, the [Antigua black pineapple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_black_pineapple "Antigua black pineapple") (_[Ananas comosus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ananas\_comosus "Ananas comosus")_), [corn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maize "Maize"), [sweet potatoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sweet_potato "Sweet potato"), [chillies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chili_pepper "Chili pepper"), [guava](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guava "Guava"), tobacco, and cotton.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-27) Later on the [Caribs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Island_Caribs "Island Caribs") settled the island.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-28)

### European rule and slavery

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Antigua_and_Barbuda&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: European rule and slavery")]

[Christopher Columbus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Columbus "Christopher Columbus") was the first European to sight the islands in 1493.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-Britannica-22)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-Commonwealth-23) The Spanish did not colonise Antigua until after a combination of European and African diseases, malnutrition, and slavery eventually extirpated most of the Native population; [smallpox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smallpox "Smallpox") was probably the greatest killer.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-29)

The English settled on Antigua in 1632;[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-Commonwealth-23)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-Britannica-22) Christopher Codrington settled on Barbuda in 1685.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-Commonwealth-23)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-Britannica-22) Tobacco and then sugar was grown, worked by a large population of slaves transported from West Africa, who soon came to vastly outnumber the European settlers.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-Britannica-22)

The English maintained control of the islands, repulsing an attempted French attack in 1666.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-Britannica-22) The brutal conditions endured by the slaves led to revolts in 1701 and 1729 and a planned revolt in 1736, the last led by [Prince Klaas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prince_Klaas "Prince Klaas"), though it was discovered before it began and the ringleaders were executed.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-30)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-31)[Slavery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slavery "Slavery") was abolished in the British Empire in 1833, affecting the economy.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-Commonwealth-23)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-Britannica-22) This was exacerbated by natural disasters such as the 1843 earthquake and the 1847 hurricane.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-Britannica-22) Mining occurred on the isle of [Redonda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Redonda "Redonda"), however, this ceased in 1929 and the island has since remained uninhabited.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-kras-2008-32)

Part of the Leeward Islands colony, Antigua and Barbuda became part of the short-lived [West Indies Federation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Indies_Federation "West Indies Federation") from 1958 to 1962.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-Commonwealth-23)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-Britannica-22)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-33) Antigua and Barbuda subsequently became an associated state of the United Kingdom with full internal autonomy on 27 February 1967.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-Britannica-22) The 1970s were dominated by discussions as to the islands' future and the rivalry between [Vere Bird](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vere_Bird "Vere Bird") of the [Antigua and Barbuda Labour Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda_Labour_Party "Antigua and Barbuda Labour Party") (ABLP) (Premier from 1967 to 1971 and 1976 to 1981) and the [Progressive Labour Movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Progressive_Labour_Movement "Progressive Labour Movement") (PLM) of [George Walter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Walter "George Walter") (Premier 1971–1976). Eventually, Antigua and Barbuda gained full independence on 1 November 1981; Vere Bird became prime minister of the new country.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-Britannica-22) The country opted to remain within the [Commonwealth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commonwealth_of_Nations "Commonwealth of Nations"), retaining [Elizabeth II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elizabeth_II "Elizabeth II") (r.1952–2022) as [head of state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monarchy_of_Antigua_and_Barbuda "Monarchy of Antigua and Barbuda"), with the first [governor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_colonial_governors_and_administrators_of_Antigua#Governors_of_Antigua_and_Barbuda_(1967%E2%80%931981) "List of colonial governors and administrators of Antigua"), [Sir Wilfred Jacobs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilfred_Jacobs "Wilfred Jacobs"), as [governor-general](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor-general_of_Antigua_and_Barbuda "Governor-general of Antigua and Barbuda"). Succeeding Wilfred Jacobs were [James Carlisle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Carlisle "James Carlisle") (1993–2007), [Louise Lake-Tack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louise_Lake-Tack "Louise Lake-Tack") (2007–2014), and the present since 2014 being [Rodney Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rodney_Williams_(governor-general) "Rodney Williams (governor-general)").

### Independence era

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Antigua_and_Barbuda&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Independence era")]

The first two decades of Antigua's independence were dominated politically by the Bird family and the ABLP, with [Vere Bird](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vere_Bird "Vere Bird") ruling from 1981 to 1994, followed by his son [Lester Bird](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lester_Bird "Lester Bird") from 1994 to 2004.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-Britannica-22) Though providing a degree of political stability, and boosting tourism to the country, the Bird governments were frequently accused of corruption, cronyism and financial malfeasance.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-Commonwealth-23)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-Britannica-22)[Vere Bird Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vere_Bird_Jr. "Vere Bird Jr."), the elder son, was forced to leave the cabinet in 1990 following a [scandal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guns_for_Antigua "Guns for Antigua") in which he was accused of smuggling Israeli weapons to Colombian drug-traffickers.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-34)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-35)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-Commonwealth-23) Another son, [Ivor Bird](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivor_Bird "Ivor Bird"), was convicted of possessing [cocaine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cocaine "Cocaine") in 1995.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-36)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-37) Also in 1995, [Hurricane Luis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Luis "Hurricane Luis") caused severe damage on Barbuda.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-38)

The ABLP's dominance of Antiguan politics ended with the [2004 Antiguan general election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_Antiguan_general_election "2004 Antiguan general election"), which was won by [Baldwin Spencer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Baldwin_Spencer "Winston Baldwin Spencer")'s [United Progressive Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Progressive_Party "United Progressive Party") (UPP).[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-Britannica-22) Winston Baldwin Spencer was [Prime Minister of Antigua and Barbuda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_Antigua_and_Barbuda "Prime Minister of Antigua and Barbuda") from 2004 to 2014.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-39) However, the UPP lost the [2014 Antiguan general election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Antiguan_general_election "2014 Antiguan general election"), with the ABLP returning to power under [Gaston Browne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaston_Browne "Gaston Browne").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-bald-40) ABLP won 15 of the 17 seats in the [2018 snap election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Antiguan_general_election "2018 Antiguan general election") under the leadership of incumbent Prime Minister Gaston Browne.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-41)

In 2015, Antigua and Barbuda established the Marine Ecosystem Protected Areas (MEPA) Trust, a mechanism for funding marine conservation and supporting local environmental efforts,[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-42) alongside the national Environmental Protection and Management Act (EPMA) to create a framework for sustaining marine protected areas and their biodiversity.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-43) In 2016, [Nelson's Dockyard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson's_Dockyard "Nelson's Dockyard") was designated as a [UNESCO World Heritage Site](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNESCO_World_Heritage_Site "UNESCO World Heritage Site").[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-44)

Most of Barbuda was devastated in early September 2017 by [Hurricane Irma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Irma "Hurricane Irma"), which brought winds with speeds reaching 295 km/h (185 mph). The storm damaged or destroyed 95% of the island's buildings and infrastructure, leaving Barbuda "barely habitable" according to Prime Minister Gaston Browne. Nearly everyone on the island was evacuated to Antigua.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-auto-45) Amidst the following rebuilding efforts on Barbuda that were estimated to cost at least $100 million,[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-time.com-46) the government announced plans to revoke a century-old law of [communal land ownership](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communal_land "Communal land") by allowing residents to buy land; a move that has been criticised as promoting "[disaster capitalism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disaster_capitalism "Disaster capitalism")".[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-NACLA-disaster-capitalism-47)

Limestone formations, rather than volcanic activity, have had the most impact on the topography of both Antigua and Barbuda, which are both relatively low-lying islands. Boggy Peak, also known as Mt. Obama from 2008 to 2016, is the highest point on both Antigua and Barbuda. It is the remnant of a volcanic crater and rises a total of 402 meters. Boggy Peak is located in the southwest of Antigua (1,319 feet).[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-Factbook-17)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-Britannica-22)

Both of these islands have very irregularly shaped coastlines that are dotted with beaches, lagoons, and natural harbours. There are reefs and shoals that surround the islands on all sides. Because of the low amount of rainfall, there are not many streams. On neither of these islands can sufficient quantities of fresh groundwater be found.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-Factbook-17)

Redonda is a small, uninhabited island located about 40 kilometres (25 miles) to the south-west of Antigua. Redonda is a rocky island.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-Britannica-22)

In Antigua and Barbuda, [forest cover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forest_cover "Forest cover") is about 18% of the total land area, equivalent to 8,120 ha of forests in 2020, down from 10,110 ha in 1990.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-49)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-50)

### Islands

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Antigua_and_Barbuda&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Islands")]

Further information: [List of islands of Antigua and Barbuda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_islands_of_Antigua_and_Barbuda "List of islands of Antigua and Barbuda")

Antigua and Barbuda consists mostly of its two namesake islands, [Antigua](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua "Antigua"), and [Barbuda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbuda "Barbuda"). Other than that, Antigua and Barbuda's biggest islands are Guiana Island and Long Island off the coast of Antigua, and [Redonda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Redonda "Redonda") island, which is far from both of the main islands.

### Climate

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Antigua_and_Barbuda&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Climate")]

Rainfall averages 990 mm (39 in) per year, with the amount varying widely from season to season. In general, the wettest period is between September and November. The islands generally experience low humidity and recurrent droughts. Temperatures average 27°C (80.6°F), with a range from 23°C (73.4°F) to 29°C (84.2°F) in the winter to from 25°C (77.0°F) to 30°C (86.0°F) in the summer and autumn. The coolest period is between December and February.

[Hurricanes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane "Hurricane") are common, including the powerful [Category 5](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Category_5_hurricane "Category 5 hurricane")[Hurricane Irma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Irma "Hurricane Irma"), on 6 September 2017, which damaged 95% of the structures on Barbuda.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-51) Some 1,800 people were evacuated to Antigua.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-52)

Officials quoted by _[Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time\_(magazine) "Time (magazine)")_ indicated that over $100 million would be required to rebuild homes and infrastructure. Philmore Mullin, Director of Barbuda's National Office of Disaster Services, said that "all critical infrastructure and utilities are non-existent – food supply, medicine, shelter, electricity, water, communications, waste management". He summarised the situation as follows: "Public utilities need to be rebuilt in their entirety... It is optimistic to think anything can be rebuilt in six months ... In my 25 years in disaster management, I have never seen something like this."[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-53)

### Environmental issues

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Antigua_and_Barbuda&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Environmental issues")]

This section is an excerpt from [Environmental issues in Antigua and Barbuda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Environmental_issues_in_Antigua_and_Barbuda "Environmental issues in Antigua and Barbuda").[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Environmental_issues_in_Antigua_and_Barbuda&action=edit)]

Like other [island nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Island_country "Island country"), Antigua and Barbuda faces unique environmental issues created by its proximity to the ocean, and small size. These include pressures on drinking water resources, natural ecosystems, and deforestation more generally.

Existing issues on the island are further made worse by [climate change](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Climate_change "Climate change"), where, not unlike other [island nations affected by climate change](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Effects_of_climate_change_on_island_nations "Effects of climate change on island nations"), [sea level rise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_level_rise "Sea level rise") and increased weather variability, create increased pressures on the communities on the islands and the land, through processes like [coastal erosion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coastal_erosion "Coastal erosion") and [saltwater intrusion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saltwater_intrusion "Saltwater intrusion").[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-54)

Not only do these issues threaten the residents of the island, but also interfere with the economy– where tourism is 80% of the GDP.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-Environmental_issues_in_Antigua_and_Barbuda_:1-55) The 2017 hurricane season was particularly destructive, with [Hurricane Maria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Maria "Hurricane Maria") and [Hurricane Irma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Irma "Hurricane Irma"), repeatedly damaging vulnerable infrastructure on the islands of Antigua and Barbuda.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-56)

Antigua and Barbuda is a [unitary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unitary_state "Unitary state")[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-57)[parliamentary democracy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parliamentary_democracy "Parliamentary democracy") under a [constitutional monarchy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitutional_monarchy "Constitutional monarchy").[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-58) The current [Constitution of Antigua and Barbuda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitution_of_Antigua_and_Barbuda "Constitution of Antigua and Barbuda") was adopted upon independence on 1 November 1981.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-:0-59) This replaced the pre-independence constitution of the [Associated State of Antigua](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Associated_State_of_Antigua "Associated State of Antigua"), which did not thoroughly define the relationship between the two islands.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-Constitution_Order_1967-60) The island of Barbuda maintains much autonomy, while the island of Antigua is directly governed by the national government.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-:0-59)

The executive branch has two primary leaders. The [Governor-General](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor-General_of_Antigua_and_Barbuda "Governor-General of Antigua and Barbuda"), currently [Rodney Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rodney_Williams_(governor-general) "Rodney Williams (governor-general)"), exercises the functions of the [Monarch of Antigua and Barbuda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monarchy_of_Antigua_and_Barbuda "Monarchy of Antigua and Barbuda"), in whom executive power is vested. The Governor-General serves at the pleasure of the Monarch,[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-:0-59) and usually serves a similar term to that of the [Prime Minister](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_Antigua_and_Barbuda "Prime Minister of Antigua and Barbuda"). The Prime Minister, currently [Gaston Browne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaston_Browne "Gaston Browne"), is the [head of government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Head_of_government "Head of government"), and is appointed by the Governor-General. The Prime Minister must be a member of the [House of Representatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Representatives_(Antigua_and_Barbuda) "House of Representatives (Antigua and Barbuda)"), and must be the member of the House of Representatives who is most likely to command the support of the majority of members. The Governor-General has the ability to dissolve Parliament on the advice of the Prime Minister, or when the majority of the members of the House of Representatives pass a motion of no confidence, and the Prime Minister does not within seven days resign or advise the Governor-General to dissolve Parliament.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-:0-59)

The legislative power of Antigua and Barbuda is vested in Parliament, which is composed of the Monarch, the [Senate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senate_(Antigua_and_Barbuda) "Senate (Antigua and Barbuda)"), and the [House of Representatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Representatives_(Antigua_and_Barbuda) "House of Representatives (Antigua and Barbuda)"). The Senate is composed of seventeen members, who are appointed by the Governor-General. Ten of the members are appointed on the advice of the Prime Minister, these members being known as government senators. An eleventh government senator is also appointed on the advice of the Prime Minister, who must be an inhabitant of Barbuda. Four of the members are appointed on the advice of the [Leader of the Opposition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leader_of_the_Opposition_(Antigua_and_Barbuda) "Leader of the Opposition (Antigua and Barbuda)"), these senators being known as opposition senators. One of the members is appointed on the advice of the [Barbuda Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbuda_Council "Barbuda Council"), and an independent senator is appointed under the discretion of the Governor-General himself. The House of Representatives is currently composed of seventeen elected members, as well as the [Speaker of the House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speaker_of_the_House_of_Representatives_of_Antigua_and_Barbuda "Speaker of the House of Representatives of Antigua and Barbuda"), who is elected by the members of the House itself. The [Attorney General](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attorney_General_of_Antigua_and_Barbuda "Attorney General of Antigua and Barbuda"), while currently an elected member of Parliament, [Steadroy Benjamin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steadroy_Benjamin "Steadroy Benjamin"), may also be appointed to the House of Representatives as an [_ex officio_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ex_officio_member "Ex officio member") member. The Attorney-General also attends sittings of the Senate. Any bill except money bills may be introduced in either chamber: money bills may only be introduced in the House. Parliament may not amend the [Barbuda Local Government Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbuda_Local_Government_Act "Barbuda Local Government Act") without the consent of the Barbuda Council.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-:0-59)

The [judiciary of Antigua and Barbuda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judiciary_of_Antigua_and_Barbuda "Judiciary of Antigua and Barbuda") is composed of the magistrates' courts, the [Supreme Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Caribbean_Supreme_Court "Eastern Caribbean Supreme Court") including the [High Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_Court_of_Antigua_and_Barbuda "High Court of Antigua and Barbuda") and the Court of Appeal, and the [Judicial Committee of the Privy Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judicial_Committee_of_the_Privy_Council "Judicial Committee of the Privy Council"), the country's final court.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-61) Antiguan and Barbudan voters rejected [a proposal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Antiguan_constitutional_referendum "2018 Antiguan constitutional referendum") to make the [Caribbean Court of Justice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caribbean_Court_of_Justice "Caribbean Court of Justice") the final court in 2018.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-62) Antigua and Barbuda is composed of three magistrates' courts districts,[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-Code_of_Procedure_Act-63) and is part of the Eastern Caribbean Supreme Court system.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-64) The acting chief justice of the Supreme Court is [Margaret Price Findlay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Margaret_Price_Findlay "Margaret Price Findlay").

Since the 1990s, the two major parties in Antigua have been the centre-right (formerly left-wing) [Antigua and Barbuda Labour Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda_Labour_Party "Antigua and Barbuda Labour Party"), and the left-wing social democratic United Progressive Party. The Labour Party and its predecessors have traditionally been the dominant party on the national level since the [1946 general elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1946_Antiguan_general_election "1946 Antiguan general election"), with brief pauses during the [Progressive Labour Movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Progressive_Labour_Movement "Progressive Labour Movement") government (predecessor of the UPP) from 1971 to 1976, and the United Progressive Party government from 2004 until 2014.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-:3-65) On Barbuda, dominant party is traditionally the [Barbuda People's Movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbuda_People's_Movement "Barbuda People's Movement"), being the only political grouping in the Barbuda Council since [2021](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Barbuda_Council_election "2021 Barbuda Council election").[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-66)[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-:3-65)

Antigua and Barbuda is composed of [six parishes and two dependencies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parishes_and_dependencies_of_Antigua_and_Barbuda "Parishes and dependencies of Antigua and Barbuda"). [Saint John](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_John,_Antigua_and_Barbuda "Saint John, Antigua and Barbuda") is the most populous parish, home to well over half of Antigua and Barbuda's population.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-67) During colonial times, the parishes were governed by parish vestries, however, the parishes now lack any sort of government.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-:02-68) Since the 2023 general elections, various proposals have been made to establish parish councils, however, as of January 2025, none have been established.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-69)[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-70) The dependency of Redonda is part of the parish of Saint John under the [Redonda Annexation Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Redonda_Annexation_Act "Redonda Annexation Act"), in Magistrates' District "A".[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-71) Barbuda is composed of eight [districts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Districts_of_Barbuda "Districts of Barbuda") that are eventually intended to have local government powers.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-72)

**Antigua and Barbuda**[[e]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-pronounce-16) is an [archipelagic country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archipelagic_country "Archipelagic country") in the [Caribbean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caribbean "Caribbean") composed of [Antigua](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua "Antigua"), [Barbuda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbuda "Barbuda"), and [dozens of other small islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_islands_of_Antigua_and_Barbuda "List of islands of Antigua and Barbuda"). Antigua and Barbuda has a total area of 440 km 2 (170 sq mi), making it one of the smallest countries in the Caribbean. The country is mostly flat, with the highest points on Antigua being in the [Shekerley Mountains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekerley_Mountains "Shekerley Mountains") and on Barbuda the [Highlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbuda_Highlands "Barbuda Highlands"). The country has a tropical savanna climate, with pockets of tropical monsoon in Antigua's southwest. Its most populated city is [St. John's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._John's,_Antigua_and_Barbuda "St. John's, Antigua and Barbuda"), followed by [All Saints](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Saints,_Antigua_and_Barbuda "All Saints, Antigua and Barbuda") and [Bolans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bolans "Bolans"). The sole settlement in Barbuda is [Codrington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Codrington,_Antigua_and_Barbuda "Codrington, Antigua and Barbuda"). Most of the country resides in the [Central Plain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Plain_(Antigua) "Central Plain (Antigua)") that stretches from St. John's to [English Harbour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_Harbour "English Harbour").

Bounded by the [Atlantic Ocean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_Ocean "Atlantic Ocean") on the east and the [Caribbean Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caribbean_Sea "Caribbean Sea") on the west, Antigua and Barbuda is located within the [Leeward Islands moist forest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leeward_Islands_moist_forests "Leeward Islands moist forests") and [Leeward Islands xeric scrub](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leeward_Islands_xeric_scrub "Leeward Islands xeric scrub")[ecoregions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecoregion "Ecoregion"). The country shares [maritime borders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maritime_boundary "Maritime boundary") with [Anguilla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anguilla "Anguilla"), [Saint Barthélemy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Barth%C3%A9lemy "Saint Barthélemy"), and [Saint Kitts and Nevis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Kitts_and_Nevis "Saint Kitts and Nevis") to the west, [Montserrat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montserrat "Montserrat") to the southwest, and [Guadeloupe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guadeloupe "Guadeloupe") to the south. Antigua and Barbuda has numerous natural parks, including [Codrington Lagoon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Codrington_Lagoon "Codrington Lagoon"), one of the largest internal bodies of water in the [Lesser Antilles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lesser_Antilles "Lesser Antilles"). Despite its dense population, the country has large swaths of undeveloped land, however, Antigua and Barbuda has experienced many [environmental issues](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Environmental_issues_in_Antigua_and_Barbuda "Environmental issues in Antigua and Barbuda") due to [climate change](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Climate_change "Climate change").

[Hunter-gatherers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archaic_period_in_Antigua_and_Barbuda "Archaic period in Antigua and Barbuda") settled the islands starting around 3700 BC, likely arriving on canoes from Central and South America. They were followed by the [Arawaks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arawaks "Arawaks") of [Venezuela](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venezuela "Venezuela") during the [Ceramic period](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ceramic_period_in_Antigua_and_Barbuda "Ceramic period in Antigua and Barbuda"). In 1493, [Christopher Columbus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Columbus "Christopher Columbus") surveyed the island of Antigua, which resulted in an attempt at Spanish settlement in 1520. Antigua remained uncolonised until 1632 when Edward Warner and his small party created the first successful British colony. Barbuda was under the control of the [Codrington family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Codrington_baronets "Codrington baronets") until the 1860s. Antiguan independence was first proposed by [Prince Klaas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prince_Klaas "Prince Klaas") in 1728, who attempted to make the island an independent kingdom. After emancipation in 1834, Antigua's autonomy slowly increased, while Barbuda was slowly integrated into Antigua. The first democratic elections were held in 1951, and by 1981, Antigua and Barbuda was independent. From 1960 until 2004, the Bird family dominated the [archipelago's politics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Politics_of_Antigua_and_Barbuda "Politics of Antigua and Barbuda") with only one interruption, which ended with the election of [Baldwin Spencer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baldwin_Spencer "Baldwin Spencer") to the premiership.

[Since 2014](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Antigua_and_Barbuda_(2014%E2%80%93present) "History of Antigua and Barbuda (2014–present)"), the [Labour Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda_Labour_Party "Antigua and Barbuda Labour Party") has dominated national politics. Antigua and Barbuda is a member of the [Commonwealth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commonwealth_of_Nations "Commonwealth of Nations") and a [Commonwealth realm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commonwealth_realm "Commonwealth realm"), being a [constitutional monarchy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitutional_monarchy "Constitutional monarchy") with [Charles III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_III "Charles III") as its head of state. The country is a [unitary state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unitary_state "Unitary state"), with Barbuda being administered by the [Barbuda Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbuda_Council "Barbuda Council") since 1976. Antigua is divided into six [parishes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parishes_of_Antigua "Parishes of Antigua"). The [central government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_Antigua_and_Barbuda "Government of Antigua and Barbuda") is composed of three main branches: [legislative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parliament_of_Antigua_and_Barbuda "Parliament of Antigua and Barbuda"), [executive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabinet_of_Antigua_and_Barbuda "Cabinet of Antigua and Barbuda"), and [judicial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judiciary_of_Antigua_and_Barbuda "Judiciary of Antigua and Barbuda"). It has a [bicameral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bicameralism "Bicameralism") national legislature comprising the directly elected [House of Representatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Representatives_(Antigua_and_Barbuda) "House of Representatives (Antigua and Barbuda)") and the [Senate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senate_(Antigua_and_Barbuda) "Senate (Antigua and Barbuda)") appointed by the [Governor-General](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor-General_of_Antigua_and_Barbuda "Governor-General of Antigua and Barbuda"), the representative of the monarch. The Labour Party and the [United Progressive Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Progressive_Party "United Progressive Party") have dominated the country's politics since [1994](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_Antiguan_general_election "1994 Antiguan general election"). The country has a [proportionally high foreign-born population](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_sovereign_states_by_immigrant_and_emigrant_population "List of sovereign states by immigrant and emigrant population"); most people are [of African descent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afro%E2%80%93Antiguans_and_Barbudans "Afro–Antiguans and Barbudans"), with significant populations of [Europeans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Antiguans_and_Barbudans "White Antiguans and Barbudans"), [Hispanics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hispanic_Antiguans_and_Barbudans "Hispanic Antiguans and Barbudans"), and [Indians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Antiguans_and_Barbudans "Indian Antiguans and Barbudans"). The country is majority Christian, with most being [Protestant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protestant "Protestant"). The most spoken home language in the country is [Antiguan and Barbudan Creole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antiguan_and_Barbudan_Creole "Antiguan and Barbudan Creole"). Compared to neighboring countries, Antigua and Barbuda [ranks highly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_rankings_of_Antigua_and_Barbuda "International rankings of Antigua and Barbuda") in most economic indicators, and ranks about average in political freedoms.

Antigua and Barbuda is a high-income country and is the most developed country in the Caribbean by [Human Development Index](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_Development_Index "Human Development Index"). It is a member of the [United Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations "United Nations"), the [OECS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OECS "OECS"), the [Regional Security System](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regional_Security_System "Regional Security System"), [CARICOM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CARICOM "CARICOM"), and the [World Trade Organisation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Trade_Organization "World Trade Organization"). Antigua and Barbuda is one of the only countries in the Caribbean to maintain an [air force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda_Defence_Force_Air_Wing "Antigua and Barbuda Defence Force Air Wing"), and has a mostly service-based [economy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economy_of_Antigua_and_Barbuda "Economy of Antigua and Barbuda"). Antigua and Barbuda maintains significant influence in the former [British Leeward Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Leeward_Islands "British Leeward Islands") and the eastern Caribbean, having the largest economy and population in the former colony. However, the country continues to struggle with human rights and political polarisation, with [declining freedom of the press](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_rights_in_Antigua_and_Barbuda#Freedom_of_the_press "Human rights in Antigua and Barbuda") and a significant [Barbudan independence movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbudan_independence_movement "Barbudan independence movement") re-emerging due to [tensions between the islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbuda_crisis "Barbuda crisis").

## Etymology

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Antigua_and_Barbuda&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Etymology")]

_Antigua_ is Spanish for 'ancient' and _barbuda_ is Spanish for 'bearded'.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-Factbook-17) The island of Antigua was originally called _Waladli_ by the [Arawaks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arawak "Arawak"), and the [Caribs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Island_Caribs "Island Caribs") possibly called Barbuda _Wa'omoni_. [Christopher Columbus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Columbus "Christopher Columbus"), while sailing by in 1493, may have named it _Santa Maria la Antigua_, after an icon in the Spanish [Seville Cathedral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seville_Cathedral "Seville Cathedral"). The "bearded" of Barbuda is thought to refer either to the male inhabitants of the island, or the bearded fig trees present there.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-18) The term _Wadadli_ is a corrupted form of the original Arawak name, emerging from a misspelling in a popular 1970s song. The term is sometimes used in Antiguan and Barbudan Creole to refer to the island's original name.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-19)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-Reg-20)_Aanteega an' Baabyuuda_ is the Creole endonym for the country, deriving from the English name.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-21)

### Pre-colonial period

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Antigua_and_Barbuda&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Pre-colonial period")]

Main article: [Pre-Columbian Antigua and Barbuda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pre-Columbian_Antigua_and_Barbuda "Pre-Columbian Antigua and Barbuda")

[Archaic-period](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archaic_period_in_Antigua_and_Barbuda "Archaic period in Antigua and Barbuda") hunter-gatherers called the [Ciboney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ciboney "Ciboney") were the first culture present in Antigua and Barbuda.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-Factbook-17)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-Britannica-22)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-Commonwealth-23)[Carbon dating](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radiocarbon_dating "Radiocarbon dating") has established the earliest settlements started around 3700 BC.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-24)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-:23-25) They were succeeded by the ceramic age pre-Columbian [Arawak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arawakan_languages "Arawakan languages")-speaking [Saladoid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saladoid "Saladoid") people who migrated from the lower [Orinoco River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orinoco_River "Orinoco River").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-26) They introduced agriculture, raising, among other crops, the [Antigua black pineapple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_black_pineapple "Antigua black pineapple") (_[Ananas comosus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ananas\_comosus "Ananas comosus")_), [corn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maize "Maize"), [sweet potatoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sweet_potato "Sweet potato"), [chillies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chili_pepper "Chili pepper"), [guava](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guava "Guava"), tobacco, and cotton.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-27) Later on the [Caribs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Island_Caribs "Island Caribs") settled the island.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-28)

### European rule and slavery

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Antigua_and_Barbuda&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: European rule and slavery")]

[Christopher Columbus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Columbus "Christopher Columbus") was the first European to sight the islands in 1493.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-Britannica-22)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-Commonwealth-23) The Spanish did not colonise Antigua until after a combination of European and African diseases, malnutrition, and slavery eventually extirpated most of the Native population; [smallpox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smallpox "Smallpox") was probably the greatest killer.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-29)

The English settled on Antigua in 1632;[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-Commonwealth-23)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-Britannica-22) Christopher Codrington settled on Barbuda in 1685.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-Commonwealth-23)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-Britannica-22) Tobacco and then sugar was grown, worked by a large population of slaves transported from West Africa, who soon came to vastly outnumber the European settlers.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-Britannica-22)

The English maintained control of the islands, repulsing an attempted French attack in 1666.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-Britannica-22) The brutal conditions endured by the slaves led to revolts in 1701 and 1729 and a planned revolt in 1736, the last led by [Prince Klaas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prince_Klaas "Prince Klaas"), though it was discovered before it began and the ringleaders were executed.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-30)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-31)[Slavery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slavery "Slavery") was abolished in the British Empire in 1833, affecting the economy.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-Commonwealth-23)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-Britannica-22) This was exacerbated by natural disasters such as the 1843 earthquake and the 1847 hurricane.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-Britannica-22) Mining occurred on the isle of [Redonda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Redonda "Redonda"), however, this ceased in 1929 and the island has since remained uninhabited.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-kras-2008-32)

Part of the Leeward Islands colony, Antigua and Barbuda became part of the short-lived [West Indies Federation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Indies_Federation "West Indies Federation") from 1958 to 1962.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-Commonwealth-23)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-Britannica-22)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-33) Antigua and Barbuda subsequently became an associated state of the United Kingdom with full internal autonomy on 27 February 1967.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-Britannica-22) The 1970s were dominated by discussions as to the islands' future and the rivalry between [Vere Bird](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vere_Bird "Vere Bird") of the [Antigua and Barbuda Labour Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda_Labour_Party "Antigua and Barbuda Labour Party") (ABLP) (Premier from 1967 to 1971 and 1976 to 1981) and the [Progressive Labour Movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Progressive_Labour_Movement "Progressive Labour Movement") (PLM) of [George Walter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Walter "George Walter") (Premier 1971–1976). Eventually, Antigua and Barbuda gained full independence on 1 November 1981; Vere Bird became prime minister of the new country.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-Britannica-22) The country opted to remain within the [Commonwealth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commonwealth_of_Nations "Commonwealth of Nations"), retaining [Elizabeth II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elizabeth_II "Elizabeth II") (r.1952–2022) as [head of state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monarchy_of_Antigua_and_Barbuda "Monarchy of Antigua and Barbuda"), with the first [governor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_colonial_governors_and_administrators_of_Antigua#Governors_of_Antigua_and_Barbuda_(1967%E2%80%931981) "List of colonial governors and administrators of Antigua"), [Sir Wilfred Jacobs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilfred_Jacobs "Wilfred Jacobs"), as [governor-general](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor-general_of_Antigua_and_Barbuda "Governor-general of Antigua and Barbuda"). Succeeding Wilfred Jacobs were [James Carlisle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Carlisle "James Carlisle") (1993–2007), [Louise Lake-Tack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louise_Lake-Tack "Louise Lake-Tack") (2007–2014), and the present since 2014 being [Rodney Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rodney_Williams_(governor-general) "Rodney Williams (governor-general)").

### Independence era

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Antigua_and_Barbuda&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Independence era")]

The first two decades of Antigua's independence were dominated politically by the Bird family and the ABLP, with [Vere Bird](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vere_Bird "Vere Bird") ruling from 1981 to 1994, followed by his son [Lester Bird](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lester_Bird "Lester Bird") from 1994 to 2004.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-Britannica-22) Though providing a degree of political stability, and boosting tourism to the country, the Bird governments were frequently accused of corruption, cronyism and financial malfeasance.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-Commonwealth-23)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-Britannica-22)[Vere Bird Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vere_Bird_Jr. "Vere Bird Jr."), the elder son, was forced to leave the cabinet in 1990 following a [scandal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guns_for_Antigua "Guns for Antigua") in which he was accused of smuggling Israeli weapons to Colombian drug-traffickers.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-34)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-35)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-Commonwealth-23) Another son, [Ivor Bird](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivor_Bird "Ivor Bird"), was convicted of possessing [cocaine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cocaine "Cocaine") in 1995.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-36)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-37) Also in 1995, [Hurricane Luis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Luis "Hurricane Luis") caused severe damage on Barbuda.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-38)

The ABLP's dominance of Antiguan politics ended with the [2004 Antiguan general election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_Antiguan_general_election "2004 Antiguan general election"), which was won by [Baldwin Spencer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Baldwin_Spencer "Winston Baldwin Spencer")'s [United Progressive Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Progressive_Party "United Progressive Party") (UPP).[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-Britannica-22) Winston Baldwin Spencer was [Prime Minister of Antigua and Barbuda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_Antigua_and_Barbuda "Prime Minister of Antigua and Barbuda") from 2004 to 2014.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-39) However, the UPP lost the [2014 Antiguan general election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Antiguan_general_election "2014 Antiguan general election"), with the ABLP returning to power under [Gaston Browne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaston_Browne "Gaston Browne").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-bald-40) ABLP won 15 of the 17 seats in the [2018 snap election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Antiguan_general_election "2018 Antiguan general election") under the leadership of incumbent Prime Minister Gaston Browne.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-41)

In 2015, Antigua and Barbuda established the Marine Ecosystem Protected Areas (MEPA) Trust, a mechanism for funding marine conservation and supporting local environmental efforts,[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-42) alongside the national Environmental Protection and Management Act (EPMA) to create a framework for sustaining marine protected areas and their biodiversity.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-43) In 2016, [Nelson's Dockyard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson's_Dockyard "Nelson's Dockyard") was designated as a [UNESCO World Heritage Site](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNESCO_World_Heritage_Site "UNESCO World Heritage Site").[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-44)

Most of Barbuda was devastated in early September 2017 by [Hurricane Irma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Irma "Hurricane Irma"), which brought winds with speeds reaching 295 km/h (185 mph). The storm damaged or destroyed 95% of the island's buildings and infrastructure, leaving Barbuda "barely habitable" according to Prime Minister Gaston Browne. Nearly everyone on the island was evacuated to Antigua.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-auto-45) Amidst the following rebuilding efforts on Barbuda that were estimated to cost at least $100 million,[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-time.com-46) the government announced plans to revoke a century-old law of [communal land ownership](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communal_land "Communal land") by allowing residents to buy land; a move that has been criticised as promoting "[disaster capitalism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disaster_capitalism "Disaster capitalism")".[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-NACLA-disaster-capitalism-47)

Limestone formations, rather than volcanic activity, have had the most impact on the topography of both Antigua and Barbuda, which are both relatively low-lying islands. Boggy Peak, also known as Mt. Obama from 2008 to 2016, is the highest point on both Antigua and Barbuda. It is the remnant of a volcanic crater and rises a total of 402 meters. Boggy Peak is located in the southwest of Antigua (1,319 feet).[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-Factbook-17)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-Britannica-22)

Both of these islands have very irregularly shaped coastlines that are dotted with beaches, lagoons, and natural harbours. There are reefs and shoals that surround the islands on all sides. Because of the low amount of rainfall, there are not many streams. On neither of these islands can sufficient quantities of fresh groundwater be found.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-Factbook-17)

Redonda is a small, uninhabited island located about 40 kilometres (25 miles) to the south-west of Antigua. Redonda is a rocky island.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-Britannica-22)

In Antigua and Barbuda, [forest cover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forest_cover "Forest cover") is about 18% of the total land area, equivalent to 8,120 ha of forests in 2020, down from 10,110 ha in 1990.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-49)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-50)

Antigua and Barbuda consists mostly of its two namesake islands, [Antigua](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua "Antigua"), and [Barbuda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbuda "Barbuda"). Other than that, Antigua and Barbuda's biggest islands are Guiana Island and Long Island off the coast of Antigua, and [Redonda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Redonda "Redonda") island, which is far from both of the main islands.

### Climate

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Antigua_and_Barbuda&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Climate")]

Rainfall averages 990 mm (39 in) per year, with the amount varying widely from season to season. In general, the wettest period is between September and November. The islands generally experience low humidity and recurrent droughts. Temperatures average 27°C (80.6°F), with a range from 23°C (73.4°F) to 29°C (84.2°F) in the winter to from 25°C (77.0°F) to 30°C (86.0°F) in the summer and autumn. The coolest period is between December and February.

[Hurricanes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane "Hurricane") are common, including the powerful [Category 5](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Category_5_hurricane "Category 5 hurricane")[Hurricane Irma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Irma "Hurricane Irma"), on 6 September 2017, which damaged 95% of the structures on Barbuda.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-51) Some 1,800 people were evacuated to Antigua.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-52)

Officials quoted by _[Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time\_(magazine) "Time (magazine)")_ indicated that over $100 million would be required to rebuild homes and infrastructure. Philmore Mullin, Director of Barbuda's National Office of Disaster Services, said that "all critical infrastructure and utilities are non-existent – food supply, medicine, shelter, electricity, water, communications, waste management". He summarised the situation as follows: "Public utilities need to be rebuilt in their entirety... It is optimistic to think anything can be rebuilt in six months ... In my 25 years in disaster management, I have never seen something like this."[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-53)

### Environmental issues

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Antigua_and_Barbuda&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Environmental issues")]

This section is an excerpt from [Environmental issues in Antigua and Barbuda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Environmental_issues_in_Antigua_and_Barbuda "Environmental issues in Antigua and Barbuda").[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Environmental_issues_in_Antigua_and_Barbuda&action=edit)]

Like other [island nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Island_country "Island country"), Antigua and Barbuda faces unique environmental issues created by its proximity to the ocean, and small size. These include pressures on drinking water resources, natural ecosystems, and deforestation more generally.

Existing issues on the island are further made worse by [climate change](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Climate_change "Climate change"), where, not unlike other [island nations affected by climate change](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Effects_of_climate_change_on_island_nations "Effects of climate change on island nations"), [sea level rise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_level_rise "Sea level rise") and increased weather variability, create increased pressures on the communities on the islands and the land, through processes like [coastal erosion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coastal_erosion "Coastal erosion") and [saltwater intrusion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saltwater_intrusion "Saltwater intrusion").[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-54)

Not only do these issues threaten the residents of the island, but also interfere with the economy– where tourism is 80% of the GDP.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-Environmental_issues_in_Antigua_and_Barbuda_:1-55) The 2017 hurricane season was particularly destructive, with [Hurricane Maria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Maria "Hurricane Maria") and [Hurricane Irma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Irma "Hurricane Irma"), repeatedly damaging vulnerable infrastructure on the islands of Antigua and Barbuda.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-56)

### Government

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Antigua_and_Barbuda&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Government")]

Antigua and Barbuda is a [unitary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unitary_state "Unitary state")[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-57)[parliamentary democracy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parliamentary_democracy "Parliamentary democracy") under a [constitutional monarchy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitutional_monarchy "Constitutional monarchy").[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-58) The current [Constitution of Antigua and Barbuda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitution_of_Antigua_and_Barbuda "Constitution of Antigua and Barbuda") was adopted upon independence on 1 November 1981.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-:0-59) This replaced the pre-independence constitution of the [Associated State of Antigua](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Associated_State_of_Antigua "Associated State of Antigua"), which did not thoroughly define the relationship between the two islands.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-Constitution_Order_1967-60) The island of Barbuda maintains much autonomy, while the island of Antigua is directly governed by the national government.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-:0-59)

The executive branch has two primary leaders. The [Governor-General](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor-General_of_Antigua_and_Barbuda "Governor-General of Antigua and Barbuda"), currently [Rodney Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rodney_Williams_(governor-general) "Rodney Williams (governor-general)"), exercises the functions of the [Monarch of Antigua and Barbuda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monarchy_of_Antigua_and_Barbuda "Monarchy of Antigua and Barbuda"), in whom executive power is vested. The Governor-General serves at the pleasure of the Monarch,[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-:0-59) and usually serves a similar term to that of the [Prime Minister](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_Antigua_and_Barbuda "Prime Minister of Antigua and Barbuda"). The Prime Minister, currently [Gaston Browne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaston_Browne "Gaston Browne"), is the [head of government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Head_of_government "Head of government"), and is appointed by the Governor-General. The Prime Minister must be a member of the [House of Representatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Representatives_(Antigua_and_Barbuda) "House of Representatives (Antigua and Barbuda)"), and must be the member of the House of Representatives who is most likely to command the support of the majority of members. The Governor-General has the ability to dissolve Parliament on the advice of the Prime Minister, or when the majority of the members of the House of Representatives pass a motion of no confidence, and the Prime Minister does not within seven days resign or advise the Governor-General to dissolve Parliament.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-:0-59)

The legislative power of Antigua and Barbuda is vested in Parliament, which is composed of the Monarch, the [Senate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senate_(Antigua_and_Barbuda) "Senate (Antigua and Barbuda)"), and the [House of Representatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Representatives_(Antigua_and_Barbuda) "House of Representatives (Antigua and Barbuda)"). The Senate is composed of seventeen members, who are appointed by the Governor-General. Ten of the members are appointed on the advice of the Prime Minister, these members being known as government senators. An eleventh government senator is also appointed on the advice of the Prime Minister, who must be an inhabitant of Barbuda. Four of the members are appointed on the advice of the [Leader of the Opposition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leader_of_the_Opposition_(Antigua_and_Barbuda) "Leader of the Opposition (Antigua and Barbuda)"), these senators being known as opposition senators. One of the members is appointed on the advice of the [Barbuda Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbuda_Council "Barbuda Council"), and an independent senator is appointed under the discretion of the Governor-General himself. The House of Representatives is currently composed of seventeen elected members, as well as the [Speaker of the House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speaker_of_the_House_of_Representatives_of_Antigua_and_Barbuda "Speaker of the House of Representatives of Antigua and Barbuda"), who is elected by the members of the House itself. The [Attorney General](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attorney_General_of_Antigua_and_Barbuda "Attorney General of Antigua and Barbuda"), while currently an elected member of Parliament, [Steadroy Benjamin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steadroy_Benjamin "Steadroy Benjamin"), may also be appointed to the House of Representatives as an [_ex officio_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ex_officio_member "Ex officio member") member. The Attorney-General also attends sittings of the Senate. Any bill except money bills may be introduced in either chamber: money bills may only be introduced in the House. Parliament may not amend the [Barbuda Local Government Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbuda_Local_Government_Act "Barbuda Local Government Act") without the consent of the Barbuda Council.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-:0-59)

The [judiciary of Antigua and Barbuda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judiciary_of_Antigua_and_Barbuda "Judiciary of Antigua and Barbuda") is composed of the magistrates' courts, the [Supreme Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Caribbean_Supreme_Court "Eastern Caribbean Supreme Court") including the [High Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_Court_of_Antigua_and_Barbuda "High Court of Antigua and Barbuda") and the Court of Appeal, and the [Judicial Committee of the Privy Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judicial_Committee_of_the_Privy_Council "Judicial Committee of the Privy Council"), the country's final court.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-61) Antiguan and Barbudan voters rejected [a proposal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Antiguan_constitutional_referendum "2018 Antiguan constitutional referendum") to make the [Caribbean Court of Justice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caribbean_Court_of_Justice "Caribbean Court of Justice") the final court in 2018.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-62) Antigua and Barbuda is composed of three magistrates' courts districts,[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-Code_of_Procedure_Act-63) and is part of the Eastern Caribbean Supreme Court system.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-64) The acting chief justice of the Supreme Court is [Margaret Price Findlay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Margaret_Price_Findlay "Margaret Price Findlay").

Since the 1990s, the two major parties in Antigua have been the centre-right (formerly left-wing) [Antigua and Barbuda Labour Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda_Labour_Party "Antigua and Barbuda Labour Party"), and the left-wing social democratic United Progressive Party. The Labour Party and its predecessors have traditionally been the dominant party on the national level since the [1946 general elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1946_Antiguan_general_election "1946 Antiguan general election"), with brief pauses during the [Progressive Labour Movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Progressive_Labour_Movement "Progressive Labour Movement") government (predecessor of the UPP) from 1971 to 1976, and the United Progressive Party government from 2004 until 2014.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-:3-65) On Barbuda, dominant party is traditionally the [Barbuda People's Movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbuda_People's_Movement "Barbuda People's Movement"), being the only political grouping in the Barbuda Council since [2021](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Barbuda_Council_election "2021 Barbuda Council election").[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-66)[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda#cite_note-:3-65)
